title: Comparative two-dimensional fluorescence gel electrophoresis
protocol: Combine protein stock solutions to make a 100 µl aliquot pool.
Heat 45 µl of the aliquot pool in a thermoshaker for 4 min at 95°C.
Incubate 45 µl (51.53 µg) of the denatured aliquot pool with 1 µl Sci 3 for 30 min on ice.
Stop labeling by adding 1 µl lysine solution and incubating for 10 min on ice.
Rinse Pall 3K filter units three times with cleaning solvent (500 µl each, centrifuge at 12,500 x g for 5 min).
Transfer labeled grid mix to the filter unit and centrifuge (15 min, 12,500 x g, 20°C).
Add 100 µl reducing buffer to the mixture.
Vortex the mixture for 45 min at 1,000 rpm.
Centrifuge the mixture (15 min, 12,500 x g, 20°C).
Add 100 µl alkylation buffer to the filter unit and vortex in the dark (1,000 rpm, 30 min).
Stop the process by centrifuging (15 min, 12,500 x g, 20°C) and rinsing with quenching buffer (100 µl; vortex for 15 min at 1,000 rpm; centrifuge for 30 min, 12,500 x g, 4°C).
Add 100 µl Tris buffer to the filter unit and vortex (45 min, 1,000 rpm).
Transfer the protein solution to a fresh tube.
Lyse E. coli (25 mg) in 1 ml lysis buffer containing 1/10 tablet EDTA-free protease inhibitor cocktail Complete mini.
Vortex (30 min) and centrifuge (12,000 x g, 4°C).
Adjust the supernatant to pH 8-9.
Determine the protein concentration at 590 nm using the Bradford-based Cytoskeleton kit ADV01.
Label E. coli lysate with 1 µl of Sci 5.
Quench the reaction with 1 µl lysine solution.
Add IEF buffer to the lysate at a 1:1 ratio.
Vortex the mixture and centrifuge for 1 minute each.
Prepare a trough in the rehydration tray with 450 µl rehydration buffer for passive rehydration of the IPG strip overnight.
Place the IPG-strip into the trough gel side down and overlay it with 3 ml mineral oil.
If cup-loading is used, place the IPG strip gel side up into the manifold.
Pipette the sample (13.2 µl) followed by mineral oil (10 µl) into a cup located on the anodic side of the strip.
Ensure identical protein amounts per strip for multiple parallel experiments.
Perform focusing at 20°C and 50 µA for 20 hours with specified voltage steps.
Equilibrate the IPG-strip in equilibration buffer I for 15 minutes.
Equilibrate the IPG-strip in equilibration buffer II for 15 minutes.
Place two electrode wicks into the wick tray.
Add 45 ml SERVA cathode buffer to one electrode wick.
Add 45 ml SERVA anode buffer to the other electrode wick.
Allow 15 min for buffer uptake.
Spread cooling fluid (3 ml) on the cooling plate of one drawer of the FlatTop Tower.
Load molecular weight marker Serva Triple Color Protein Standard III (5 µl; prestained protein ladder) into the dedicated well of the gel.
Place the IPG strip into the designated trough face-down with the anode (+) side towards this marker well.
Apply 0.5 µl labeled grid mix to each reference well immediately before starting the second electrophoresis dimension.
Perform the second dimension for ~6 hours at specified conditions:
Start with 100 V, 7 mA, 1 W for 30 min; then 200 V, 13 mA, 3 W for 30 min; followed by 300 V, 20 mA, 5 W for 10 min.
Pause the power supply and remove the pI-strip.
Restart the power supply at 1.5 kV, 40 mA, 30 W for 230 min; then continue with 1.5 kV, 50 mA, 40 W for 40 min.
Stop the experiment when the running front reaches the end of the gel.
Scan gels immediately using the green laser for Sci 3.
Set emission filter to 580 and band pass (BP) to 30, with photomultiplier tube (PMT) at 525 for the green laser.
Use the red laser for G-Dye300.
Set emission filter to 670 and BP to 30, with PMT at 490 for the red laser.
Set resolution for main scans to 100 µm per pixel.
Adapt PMT response so that gel image shows the most intense protein spot slightly below saturation.
Visualize gel images using ImageQuant software.
Store visualized gel images.
Apply the determined gel match vectors to the analyte proteome on the gel.
Control the mapping of the match vectors manually.
